title: Golden test for build-deck.js (deck JSON -> report + HTML snapshot)
description: scripts/build-deck.js has no automated test. examples/2026-06-28.deck.json is said to reproduce the hand-built 36-slide deck identically, but nothing enforces it. bs-ixn changes the skill that feeds this script and will likely extend the report, so lock the deterministic substrate first: build the example deck, snapshot report + HTML, fail on drift. Also covers the cardinal-rule enforcement (placeholder lyrics / unknown song / unknown section must be a build ERROR, not a slide).
acceptance_criteria: Running the suite builds examples/2026-06-28.deck.json and compares report + HTML against checked-in goldens; a deck with placeholder lyrics, an unknown song, and an unknown section each fail the build with a named segment.
close_reason: Done: tests/build-deck.test.js (9 tests, node:test, no new deps) + goldens. npm test / npm run test:update. Surfaced the bs-fdn divergence in the reference deck.

title: Set Gmail OAuth app to 'In production' — 7-day refresh-token expiry
description: The pre-existing token.json was dead with invalid_grant. Root cause: while an OAuth app's publishing status is 'Testing' in Google Cloud Console, Google expires refresh tokens after 7 DAYS. An unattended agent will therefore silently stop working every week — a miserable failure to debug on a Saturday night before a Sunday service. Set the app to 'In production' so refresh tokens are long-lived.
acceptance_criteria: OAuth app publishing status is 'In production'; the agent's token survives longer than 7 days without re-consent.
notes: OAuth app PUBLISHED by user 2026-07-11; token deleted and re-consented. Refresh verified live (rotates correctly, gmail.modify present). BUT publishing cannot be confirmed from the token — a Testing-status refresh token and a published one are indistinguishable for the first 7 days, and the failure is silent. Added agent/src/email_agent/healthcheck.py: it reports the refresh token's age and only declares the cliff cleared once the token is >=7 days old AND still valid. RE-CHECK AFTER 2026-07-18: run 'uv run python -m email_agent.healthcheck'. If it still says OK, publishing genuinely took and this can be closed.

title: Live-verify email agent against real Gmail (post-consent)
description: All of bs-tiz.1/.2/.3 is fake-driven so far: the stored refresh token was dead (invalid_grant) so nothing has touched live Gmail. Once consent is re-run, verify: (1) heartbeat --dry-run detects a real matching email; (2) get_message body extraction on a real message from the minister of music — the quoted-printable guard assumes Gmail pre-decodes body.data; (3) an actual send_reply lands as a reply IN the original thread rather than starting a new one; (4) an attachment (PDF order of service) round-trips via save_attachment.
acceptance_criteria: A real email to the inbox is detected by the gate, handled, and answered with an in-thread reply.
notes: PARTIAL live verification done 2026-07-11: Gmail auth is live (tlovetteiii@gmail.com, scope gmail.modify = read+send). Gate ran against the real inbox: 145 messages scanned, 0 actionable — the 'ignores non-matching mail' criterion is now proven live rather than against fakes. STILL UNVERIFIED: get_message body extraction on a real message, an actual in-thread send_reply, and attachment round-trip. Needs a real test email with an 'AI:' subject.
close_reason: Live-verified end-to-end on 2026-07-11: gate detected a real 'AI:' email (150 scanned, 1 actionable, correctly classified initial); get_message extracted the text/plain body and headers from a real message; the agent ran on Sonnet and sent a real reply that landed IN-THREAD (correct Re: subject + In-Reply-To); idempotency confirmed (re-run sends nothing). Attachment round-trip on a real email remains untested — no attachment was sent.

title: Spike: prove Agent SDK primitives on the host (setup-token auth + session resume + skill load)
description: Docs confirm the plumbing works; this is the short hands-on confirmation before building the harness. Using the Python Claude Agent SDK (claude-agent-sdk): (1) generate a long-lived OAuth token with 'claude setup-token', set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, and confirm a headless query bills the Claude subscription (NOT an API account) — verify ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset so it doesn't silently win; (2) run one query, capture session_id from the init SystemMessage, then resume with ClaudeAgentOptions(resume=session_id) and confirm prior context is restored across separate process invocations; (3) confirm the SDK auto-loads gen_service from .claude/ (setting_sources) and can actually run it end-to-end. Reference Anthropic's official email-assistant example in github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-demos. Outcome: a green/red on each primitive so bs-tiz.4 is built on proven ground.
acceptance_criteria: A headless claude-agent-sdk query runs against the subscription via CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; a resumed session restores prior context across two separate process runs; gen_service loads and runs from .claude/ inside an SDK query; findings recorded (esp. any auth/skill-loading gotchas).
notes: SCAFFOLDING DONE. SDK 0.2.116 installed (agent/, uv). API surface confirmed against the installed package: ClaudeAgentOptions has resume, setting_sources (Literal['user','project','local']), fork_session, model, AND a dedicated 'skills' field (relevant to bs-tiz.8). query() yields SystemMessage (init, carries session_id) / AssistantMessage / ResultMessage. Spike written at agent/spike/spike.py with 4 subcommands (auth, session-start, session-resume, skill); 'all' re-execs session-resume as a SUBPROCESS so resume is proven across genuinely separate OS processes rather than falsely passing on in-process state. BLOCKED on CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from 'claude setup-token'. Confirmed ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is unset (the billing foot-gun is not present); config.assert_subscription_auth() now enforces this at startup.
close_reason: All three assumptions GREEN. See agent/spike/FINDINGS.md. Key correction: total_cost_usd is NOT a billing signal (Claude Code reports a cost estimate regardless of which account pays); RateLimitEvent.rate_limit_type='five_hour' is positive proof of subscription billing. Session resume works across separate OS processes and keeps the same session_id. setting_sources=['project'] is required for skill loading and fails SILENTLY if omitted.

title: Reply + report composition: deck link, structured report, missing-lyrics prompt loop
description: Where most of the ideation's nuance lives — this is steering/prompt design as much as plumbing. After gen_service runs, the agent replies in-thread with: the link to the hosted deck; a structured report ('I already had verses 1-3 of Amazing Grace in the library — check my work', 'you asked for a hymn we hadn't done, I added it to the library from the Baptist Hymnal', 'check line wrapping / tell me if you want font tweaks'); and CRITICALLY a prompt-for-more-info loop when a requested song has no lyrics ('you listed At the Cross as congregational but I don't have lyrics — reply with them, and note any repeats/bridge/extra chorus you sing'). Must also handle the library-divergence case: if the minister supplies lyrics that differ from the library, use his version for THIS deck, call out the difference, and do NOT modify the library unless explicitly told to. The example replies from the ideation transcript are the behavioral spec.
acceptance_criteria: Reply is posted in-thread with a working deck link and a structured report; a song missing lyrics yields a title-only slide plus an explicit reply asking for lyrics (never fabricated); minister-supplied lyrics that differ from the library are used for the deck, flagged in the reply, and the library file is left unchanged unless explicitly requested; transcript example scenarios are captured as test cases. Optional: PDF attachment fallback for off-network recipients.
notes: Deck-link source (2026-07-16): the reply link is the publish tool's returned URL, ${DECK_BASE_URL}/decks/<date>/index.html (bs-tiz.10). DECK_BASE_URL supersedes the old PUBLIC_BASE_URL. Not a https://<host>/passages/... path.

title: Agent harness (Python Claude Agent SDK) with per-thread session resume
description: The broad 'handle-an-email' agent entry point, built on the Python Claude Agent SDK (Python chosen to match the Gmail tooling and attachment-conversion story). Launched by the dispatcher with a threadId + session_id: new session for an initiating email, resume for a reply so full prior context (including what it told the minister and his corrections) is restored. Deliberately NOT narrowed to gen_service — it is given the Gmail tools plus access to its skills and instructed to discover intent from the message and dispatch to the right skill. For this POC the one skill it drives is gen_service (invoked via its non-interactive batch contract). Architected broad so future skills slot in without rework.
design: Build on Python 'claude-agent-sdk' (Claude Code as a library). Confirmed-from-docs primitives (proven hands-on by bs-tiz.7): resume via ClaudeAgentOptions(resume=session_id), session_id captured from the init SystemMessage; gen_service auto-loads from .claude/ (setting_sources) so NO skill-invocation bridge is needed — the harness gives the model the Gmail tools + its skills and lets it dispatch. Prior art: Anthropic's official email-assistant example, github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-demos — read before building. Note AskUserQuestion is a built-in SDK tool but does NOT apply here (no interactive user) — reinforces the non-interactive/report design in bs-ixn/bs-tiz.5.
acceptance_criteria: Agent starts from a threadId+session_id; an initiating email creates a session and a reply resumes the same session with prior context intact; the agent reads the message, retrieves attachments as needed, infers intent, and invokes gen_service via the batch contract; adding a second skill later requires no change to the harness.
notes:
DONE AND LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-12 (agent/src/email_agent/harness.py). Held open only by its dependency on bs-ixn — do NOT rebuild it. Proven end-to-end: a real 'AI:' email was read, handled on Sonnet, and answered with a correct in-thread reply; session_id persisted and resumed on the next tick.

Design points that must not be regressed:
- Broad 'handle-an-email' system prompt, NOT a gen_service wrapper — adding a second skill must not require touching this file.
- setting_sources=['project'] makes .claude/ skills visible. Omit it and the agent silently has NOTHING to dispatch to — no error, it just can't see the skills.
- permission_mode='bypassPermissions' — headless, nobody can approve a tool prompt.
- A run must end in send_reply OR skip_reply (TERMINAL_TOOLS). Deciding NOTHING is the error, because the dispatcher's commit boundary would drop the request silently. (An earlier version demanded a reply; that is what made the agent answer its own mail — see bs-c8y. Do not reintroduce it.)
close_reason: Unblocked by bs-ixn and closed. Both were DONE and live-verified on 2026-07-11/12 and were only held open by their dependency on bs-ixn (batch mode), which is now complete. No further work was needed on either.

title: Deterministic Gmail tools: getMessage, listAttachments, getAttachmentBinary, sendReply
description: The narrow, deterministic tool surface the agent uses to interact with Gmail (reusing existing OAuth creds). Four tools: getMessage(msgId) → headers + body; listAttachments(msgId) → attachment metadata (filename, extension, size, mimeType); getAttachmentBinary(msgId, attachmentId) → raw bytes; sendReply(threadId, body, attachments?) → replies IN-THREAD via In-Reply-To/References so the conversation stays one thread. Deliberately does NOT convert attachments — the agent handles conversion itself (it can pip install and turn a PDF/Word doc into text/markdown as needed). Tools stop at binary + metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Agent can retrieve a message's body and headers; can list attachment metadata and fetch raw bytes for each; sendReply lands as a reply within the original thread (correct In-Reply-To/References); no format conversion happens inside the tools.
notes: CREDENTIAL FINDING (blocks live verification): the pre-existing token.json (dated Mar 2025) is DEAD — refresh fails with 'invalid_grant'. Google expires refresh tokens after 7 days while an OAuth app's publishing status is still 'Testing'. The requested scope in the file is gmail.modify (read+send), which IS sufficient for sendReply, so the design holds — but the token must be regenerated. One-time consent script written at agent/src/email_agent/authorize.py (uv run python -m email_agent.authorize). To survive unattended, the OAuth app must be set to 'In production' in Google Cloud Console, or the 7-day expiry will keep killing the agent.
close_reason: Implemented and unit-tested (40 tests green). Live Gmail verification pending credential refresh — tracked separately.

title: Dispatcher + SQLite state store (idempotency, in-flight lock, thread→session map)
description: The component the ideation implies but doesn't name. Consumes the gate's {threadId, msgId} list and owns all cross-run state in a small SQLite DB: threadId → {session_id, last_processed_msgId, status, updated_at}. For each actionable thread it (a) skips messages already acted on, (b) skips threads currently in-flight via a transactional 'claim', and (c) maps the thread to a Claude Agent SDK session_id (new for an initial message, resume for a reply). SQLite over a JSON file specifically because the heartbeat overlaps itself — slide generation can take minutes and a JSON read/write race would double-process a thread; SQLite gives a transactional claim for free. This table is the single source of truth for 'have we handled this' and 'which session belongs to this thread'.
design: SCOPE NARROWED by Agent SDK: the SDK persists the full conversation transcript as JSONL on our filesystem, so this store does NOT hold conversation history — only the mapping/bookkeeping: threadId -> {session_id, last_processed_msgId, status, updated_at}. session_id is the Agent SDK session captured from the init SystemMessage (new session for an initial email; ClaudeAgentOptions(resume=session_id) for a reply). SQLite still warranted for the transactional in-flight claim (overlapping heartbeats + minutes-long slide generation).
acceptance_criteria: A schema exists for threadId→{session_id,last_processed_msgId,status,updated_at}; re-running the heartbeat while a thread is in-flight does NOT launch a second agent for it; a reply resolves to the same session_id as its initiating message; an already-processed message is not reprocessed.
notes:
DONE AND LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-11 (store.py, dispatcher.py, heartbeat.py). Held open only by its dependency on bs-tiz.4 -> bs-ixn — do NOT rebuild it. Transactional claim is mutation-tested (swap it for read-then-write and the concurrency tests fail). Stale-claim reaping, thread→session mapping, and idempotency all proven; re-running the heartbeat on an answered thread processes 0 and sends nothing.

Two tables, both needed: processed_messages (idempotency ledger — last_processed_msg_id alone cannot prevent a duplicate reply when the gate re-emits an older message) and agent_sent_messages (authorship; surfaced to the agent as a HINT by get_thread, and a cheap dispatcher fast-path). 'We wrote it' and 'we handled it' are deliberately separate facts.
close_reason: Unblocked by bs-ixn and closed. Both were DONE and live-verified on 2026-07-11/12 and were only held open by their dependency on bs-ixn (batch mode), which is now complete. No further work was needed on either.

title: Email gate: CRON poll + subject-regex intent filter
description: Deterministic entry point for the email agent (no LLM). A heartbeat (~60s CRON for POC; later a Lambda+EventBridge timer) polls the shared Gmail inbox using existing OAuth creds and identifies ONLY messages the agent should act on. Applies a configurable subject-line regex (e.g. 'AI:', 'Calvary AI', 'media AI') and deterministically classifies initial-message vs reply (e.g. Re: / References header). Fetches metadata only, not content — its sole job is to emit a list of {threadId, msgId} for the dispatcher. Everything downstream (reading bodies, attachments, deciding intent) is left to the agent. Rationale: since the inbox is a shared personal Gmail during POC, we need a deterministic gate so the agent never 'wakes up and reads whatever is there' — it only ever acts on messages explicitly addressed to it.
acceptance_criteria: Subject pattern and poll interval are configurable; a matching new email and a matching reply are both detected and correctly classified; non-matching mail is ignored; output is a list of {threadId, msgId} with no message bodies fetched; no LLM call in this component.
close_reason: Implemented and unit-tested (40 tests green). Live Gmail verification pending credential refresh — tracked separately.

title: Deterministic build script: model emits structured data, script renders HTML
description: Today the model hand-writes slide markup and manually splices it into the template (replace the <!-- SLIDES --> line) — a large exact-syntax surface a cheap model gets subtly wrong (unclosed divs, dropped scrim, mis-padded Slide numbers). Move HTML out of the model: define a structured intermediate (JSON list of segments/slides with type + text fields) and a small deterministic build script that renders templates/service-slides-template.html from it. The model's only job becomes producing well-formed data. Foundational: also absorbs the stanza-split and slide-numbering risks.
acceptance_criteria: A documented JSON schema for the deck; a build script that renders the preview HTML from JSON deterministically; gen_service updated to emit JSON rather than raw HTML; example (2026-06-28) reproducible via the script.
close_reason: Implemented and unit-tested (40 tests green). Live Gmail verification pending credential refresh — tracked separately.

title: gen_service: library-first lyrics, no drafting-from-memory in batch mode
description: Current rule tells the model to draft copyrighted lyrics from memory and self-assess when it doesn't know — exactly the calibrated self-knowledge a small model is worst at, and the VERIFY flag is preview-only so nobody catches a hallucination in an unattended pipeline. For batch mode: project lyrics ONLY if already in songs/ or clearly public-domain-fetchable; everything else gets a title slide only and a 'needs lyrics' line in the report. Removes the fabrication surface entirely.
acceptance_criteria: In batch mode the model never invents lyrics; a song not in the library and not PD-fetchable yields a title-only slide + report entry; interactive mode may retain the drafted-with-VERIFY behavior if desired.
notes:
Why this matters more than it looks: the agent runs unattended on Sonnet with NOBODY in the loop to catch an invented verse before it reaches the sanctuary screen. gen_service.md today still permits drafting lyrics from memory for copyrighted songs (resolution rule 3: 'draft the best-known lyrics, save with verified: false'). That is defensible with a human reviewing; it is not defensible in batch mode.

Related, already handled deterministically: scripts/build-deck.js (bs-c16) now refuses placeholder/unknown sections and reports them as 'missing' rather than rendering them. See bs-1nn for the live near-miss — songs/his-name-is-jesus.md contained a literal '(paste lyrics here — song identity unconfirmed)' inside a Verse 1 section, which the old all-sections default would have projected.

Batch mode should: use the library or say 'I don't have these lyrics, send them' in the report. Never draft from memory.
close_reason: Done as part of batch mode. gen_service.md rule 3 (draft best-known lyrics from memory) is now marked INTERACTIVE ONLY; batch mode's ladder is library -> PD lookup (saved verified:false) -> title_only + ask. EVAL-PROVEN, not just documented: tests/eval/test_batch_mode.py runs the real model and asserts it. In the 7/12 run the agent wrote songs/forever-yahweh.md and songs/jesus.md with NO lyrics at all — frontmatter, a VERIFY comment, title_only in the deck, and a 'need lyrics' line in the report. It even identified Forever YHWH as Elevation Worship and recorded the copyright rather than reaching for the text.

title: gen_service: non-interactive batch mode
description: gen_service is currently built entirely around a human in the loop (ask one segment at a time, echo the running order for correction, 'ask if unsure'). The email agent has no interactive user. Add a non-interactive mode: the entire order of service arrives as one input (the emailed 'flowchart'); the model resolves everything in a single pass and NEVER blocks on a question. Anything it would have asked becomes a line in a structured report returned with the deck link (verify-these / missing-these). Biggest structural gap for the email agent and independent of model size.
acceptance_criteria: Skill documents an explicit non-interactive mode; running with a full order-of-service input produces a deck plus a report with zero blocking questions; ambiguities/missing items surface in the report, not as prompts.
notes:
DESIGN SETTLED 2026-07-12 from examples/flowcharts.md + user answers. Read that file before touching this.

REFRAME — 'zero blocking questions' in the original acceptance criteria is MISLEADING. The agent asks questions constantly; it asks them BY EMAIL. The real invariant: never block the PROCESS waiting for an answer. Every question becomes an outbound reply; the thread is the loop; session resume (bs-tiz.4) is the mechanism. Both worked examples run 3-4 rounds of refinement.

1. THE FLOWCHART IS ELLIPTICAL. It lists ONLY the music. Preshow / Welcome / video-to-sermon transition / closing prayer / ending slide are IMPLIED and must be assumed. Batch mode needs an explicit DEFAULT SERVICE SKELETON that the flowchart's music is slotted into. This is the single biggest inference the skill has to make and it is currently undocumented.

2. FLOWCHART VOCABULARY (from the two examples):
   - 'Prelude: <title> (<performer>)' -> prelude segment w/ performer
   - 'Hymns' header -> the bare titles under it are congregational (type=song)
   - 'Choir: <title>' -> special_music
   - 'Quartet' (bare) -> special_music; performer is USUALLY 'The Lovette Quartet' but NOT a given
   - 'Tehillah: <title>' + bare titles under it -> CONGREGATIONAL praise (type=song). Tehillah is the praise TEAM, not a performer. (This closed bs-fdn.)
   - 'Invitation: <title>' -> type=song, role=invitation
   - 'Video' -> video segment (black slide)
   - '<title> Nx' -> N is the NUMBER OF VERSES to sing (user-confirmed): 'America the beautiful 2x' -> sections Verse 1, Verse 2.

3. TWO TIERS OF GAP — they get DIFFERENT treatment (user-confirmed 'hold and ask first'):
   - BLOCKING (a slide cannot be sensibly made — e.g. 'Quartet' with no song title): DO NOT GENERATE. Reply asking. Generate once the answer arrives. May SUGGEST the likely answer ('The Lovette Quartet') but must not assume it.
   - NON-BLOCKING (missing lyrics for a song we cannot look up): DO generate — title_only slide — and ask for the lyrics in the same reply. One unresolved song must never cost the operator his whole deck.
   If both are present, blocking wins: hold.

4. LYRIC RESOLUTION in batch mode (this IS bs-8yd): library -> public-domain hymn lookup (store to songs/) -> otherwise title_only + ask. NEVER draft from memory. gen_service.md rule 3 (draft best-known lyrics, verified:false) must be REMOVED for batch mode. Newly looked-up lyrics are stored verified:false so they render amber and land in report.unverified[] — which IS the 'we looked these up, check them carefully' list the minister wants.

5. THE DECK IS A LIVING ARTIFACT. passages/<date>/service.deck.json is durable state. Replies amend it — observed asks: supply missing lyrics; REORDER a segment ('Star-Spangled Banner should come before the Welcome'); add a verse that was missed; add lyric slides to a choir/quartet special (use special_music's inline 'lyrics' field — do NOT pollute songs/ with performed numbers; user has no preference, inline is cleaner). Re-read the deck JSON and amend it; do NOT rebuild from the original email.

6. SERVICE DATE: the flowchart may not state it. Derive from the email (subject/body), else the next Sunday after the email date, and STATE the assumption in the reply — it drives both the output path and the season.
close_reason:
Done. gen_service.md now has an explicit Batch mode section; tests/eval/test_batch_mode.py (8 evals, all passing) exercises it against the two real flowcharts.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER READS THIS LATER: the original acceptance criterion 'zero blocking questions' was a misleading way to put it, and the implementation deliberately does NOT satisfy it literally. The agent asks questions constantly — it asks them by EMAIL. The invariant is that the PROCESS never blocks. Two tiers: a gap that makes a slide impossible (special music with no song title) HOLDS the deck and asks first; a gap that merely thins it (missing lyrics) ships a title_only slide and asks alongside. Both are proven by eval.

Also landed here: the implied service skeleton (the flowchart lists only music), the flowchart vocabulary incl. the Tehillah rule (bs-fdn), 'Nx' = N verses, and a new sermon_transition segment type — the black slide every deck needs and the reference deck was missing.

title: Email Agent: hostable slide-deck agent driven by order-of-service email
description: A small, cheaply-hostable agent that lets the minister of music email an order of service ('flowchart') and get back a link to the generated slide deck. Runs on a cheaper model (e.g. Sonnet) to control API cost. This epic collects the work to make gen_service robust enough to run unattended on a small model, plus the agent/hosting/email plumbing itself (to be fleshed out next session).
design:
HARNESS DECIDED: Claude Agent SDK (Python 'claude-agent-sdk') — Claude Code as a library, distinct from the API Tool Runner and from Managed Agents. Runs the agent loop in our own process, works on files on our infrastructure, session state as JSONL on our filesystem — matches the co-located-with-Express design (see bs-tiz.6). Docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview.

CONFIRMED FROM DOCS (bs-tiz.7 to confirm hands-on): (1) Session resume is native — capture session_id from the init SystemMessage, resume via ClaudeAgentOptions(resume=session_id); fork_session=True branches. (2) Headless auth via 'claude setup-token' -> CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (~1yr). (3) Skills/commands auto-load from .claude/ and ~/.claude/ (setting_sources) — gen_service loads natively (see bs-tiz.9 to move it to SKILL.md). Reference: official email-assistant example, github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-demos.

AUTH/ToS DECISION: run the POC on the Claude Pro subscription via OAuth token. Rationale: this is a personal-assistant agent doing a task emailed TO the operator (the volunteer PowerPoint maker), not a product offered to end users — a defensible personal use of subscription credit. WATCH: Anthropic's Agent SDK terms restrict using claude.ai login to power products for others; revisit and move to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (pay-per-token) if this is ever rolled out to serve others directly.
notes:
STATE AS OF 2026-07-12 (read this before starting anything).

THE EMAIL PLUMBING IS BUILT AND PROVEN LIVE END-TO-END. A real 'AI:' email was read from Gmail, handled by Sonnet, and answered with a correct in-thread reply; idempotent on re-run; the agent correctly DECLINES to reply when nothing is warranted. 45 tests pass (cd agent && uv run pytest). Do not rebuild any of this.

Built: agent/ (uv Python project) — gate.py, store.py, dispatcher.py, heartbeat.py, tools.py, harness.py, healthcheck.py, authorize.py. Plus scripts/build-deck.js + schemas/deck.schema.json (deterministic deck rendering).

bs-tiz.2 and bs-tiz.4 are COMPLETE but held open by their dependency on bs-ixn. Don't redo them.

WHAT'S LEFT is the SKILL side, not the plumbing: bs-ixn (non-interactive batch mode — THE critical path) -> bs-tiz.5 (reply/report composition) -> bs-tiz.6 (deployment host). bs-8yd runs parallel.

HARD-WON FACTS (all verified, don't re-derive):
1. total_cost_usd is NOT a billing signal — Claude Code reports a cost estimate regardless of which account pays. RateLimitEvent.rate_limit_type=='five_hour' is the real proof of SUBSCRIPTION billing. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY silently outranks CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; config.assert_subscription_auth() hard-fails on it.
2. setting_sources=['project'] is REQUIRED for the SDK to see .claude/ skills, and fails SILENTLY if omitted.
3. Session resume works across separate OS processes and keeps the SAME session_id.
4. AskUserQuestion must never be exposed — no interactive user, so it hangs the run.
5. THE REPLY LOOP: the agent's own reply keeps the thread subject ('Re: AI: ...') and so matches the gate regex. Neither sender nor SENT label can distinguish it (the operator tests by emailing himself — every message carries both SENT and INBOX). Fixed on TWO levels: a deterministic authorship record (store.mark_agent_sent) AND, more importantly, agent judgment — get_thread gives the whole conversation, skip_reply makes 'no reply needed' a first-class outcome. Verified with state.db DELETED: the agent still declined, reasoning from the text alone. Do not make the agent's correctness depend on the store again.
See specs/email-agent.md and agent/spike/FINDINGS.md.

title: Slide templates are ~28x larger than they need to be: 71MB first load on the minister's phone
description:
The service backgrounds are stored at ~4496x2475 as PNG despite being photographic. The slide box is 1456x816. A single real deck (examples/2026-06-28) references 12 unique templates totalling 71MB of first-load page weight — on a link whose entire purpose is a minister opening it on a phone, possibly on mobile data, in a church parking lot. templates/service/ is 188MB across 23 PNGs.

Found while building bs-tiz.10; deliberately scoped out of bs-tiz.11 (which syncs what is on disk today) so it did not grow into an image-pipeline task.
design:
THE OVERSAMPLING BUYS NOTHING — this is the fact that makes it safe. templates/service-slides-template.html:224-240 exports with html2canvas at scale:1 and encodes toBlob('image/jpeg', 0.95). So the browser ALREADY downsamples the 4496px source to the 1456x816 slide box and JPEG-encodes it. The ProPresenter slide is a 1456x816 JPEG regardless of what we upload; the extra resolution is discarded at export, not preserved.

MEASURED, not estimated: welcome-text-summer.png 17MB -> 613KB at 1456px wide, JPEG q90 (~28x). The 71MB deck becomes roughly 2-3MB. Corroboration from the repo's own assets: hymn-1.png is already 1300x720 and weighs 0.3MB — it is the model the others should follow. The outliers are the seasonal welcome cards (4 seasons x 3 styles) plus choir.png (14MB) and scripture-emphasis.png (11MB).

CAVEAT ON 1456: that width is sized for EXPORT, which is what feeds ProPresenter. A preview viewed full-screen on a large monitor CSS-scales the slide up, and a 1456px source would look slightly soft there. 2x (2912x1632) is immune to that and still ~4x smaller than today. Pick deliberately.

KEEP THE MASTERS. Do not re-encode templates/service/*.png in place — archive or keep the high-res originals and generate derived copies. Re-encoding source assets is destructive and the originals are what an operator edits.

FORMAT COUPLING: build-deck.js resolves backgrounds by NAME (e.g. hymn-1.png, SCRIM_BACKGROUNDS is a Set of .png filenames). Switching to .jpg/.webp is therefore NOT purely an asset change — it touches the renderer's filename constants and the golden tests. Keeping the .png extension on a JPEG-encoded body would render (browsers sniff) but is a lie on the wire and will confuse someone later. Decide: rename properly and update build-deck.js, or downscale-only as PNG (2.5MB for the 17MB file measured above — a 7x win with zero renderer changes, and a strictly cheaper first step).
acceptance_criteria: A published deck's first-load weight is a few MB, not 71MB. Exported JPEGs are visually indistinguishable from today's at 1456x816 (the export path re-encodes anyway). High-res masters are preserved somewhere, not destroyed. build-deck.js and its goldens still pass if filenames change.

title: Deck bucket has no CORS config; html2canvas export can taint the canvas cross-origin
description: bs-tiz.10 acceptance criteria explicitly requires the bucket (or CDN front) to return Access-Control-Allow-Origin on template-image responses, because cross-origin template images taint the html2canvas canvas and make canvas.toBlob() throw SecurityError — the Export button fails while the deck still LOOKS correct on screen. infra/ (bs-crp) ships no aws_s3_bucket_cors_configuration, so that criterion is currently unmet.
design: NUANCE WORTH KNOWING BEFORE ADDING IT: when the deck HTML is served from the bucket itself (decks/<date>/index.html) and templates live at templates/service/*.png in the SAME bucket, the images are SAME-ORIGIN and no CORS is needed — the tainting scenario does not arise on the happy path. It bites on the DEV/PREVIEW path: a locally rendered service-preview.html (file:// or localhost) built with --asset-base pointing at S3 pulls those images cross-origin and taints the canvas. So this is not a production blocker but it will bite whoever tests export locally, confusingly, because the slides render fine. Fix: aws_s3_bucket_cors_configuration allowing GET, and crossorigin=anonymous on the img tags in build-deck.js templates (CORS headers alone do not untaint — the element must opt in). Both halves are required.
acceptance_criteria: JPEG export via the Export button is verified from the hosted S3 URL AND from a locally rendered preview pointed at the S3 asset base, without SecurityError.
notes: BUCKET HALF DONE 2026-07-16 (in bs-crp / infra/s3.tf): aws_s3_bucket_cors_configuration allows GET+HEAD from any origin. allowed_origins=* is deliberate — every object is already anonymously readable via the bucket policy, so a narrower list would imply a confidentiality this bucket does not have. REMAINING: the build-deck.js half. CORS response headers alone do NOT untaint the canvas — the elements must carry crossorigin="anonymous" or the browser never sends an Origin header and S3's ACAO response goes unused. Do that in the templates build-deck.js emits, then verify export from BOTH a hosted S3 URL and a local preview pointed at the S3 asset base. || CODE DONE 2026-07-16: build-deck.js emits crossorigin="anonymous" on bg ONLY when the asset base is absolute/cross-origin (regex on scheme:// or //); same-origin default unaffected so goldens are byte-identical. Unit-tested (both modes). REMAINING: end-to-end Export verification from a hosted S3 URL + a local preview pointed at the S3 base — needs templates in the bucket (bs-tiz.11) and a browser check; converges with the bs-tiz.10 live smoke test. || 2026-07-16 (bs-tiz.10 session): CONFIRMED IN A PUBLISHED DECK — the live object at decks/2026-06-28/index.html carries 37 crossorigin="anonymous" attrs on absolute bucket-origin img srcs, so the build-deck.js half demonstrably fires on the real publish path. Export verification STILL BLOCKED on bs-tiz.11 (bucket has no templates yet, so nothing renders to export). WORTH KNOWING when that test runs: DECK_BASE_URL is the bucket's own website endpoint, so a deck served FROM the bucket loads its images SAME-ORIGIN — the crossorigin attr is harmless there (same-origin wins before the CORS check) but is also NOT exercising anything. The tainting path this issue exists for is only the LOCAL preview built with --asset-base pointing at S3. Test that one specifically; a green Export from the hosted URL alone does NOT close this issue.

title: Deck URLs are HTTP-only: S3 website endpoint can't serve the https link bs-tiz.10 promises
description: infra/ (bs-crp) configures cbc-wilm-agent-public via aws_s3_bucket_website_configuration, whose endpoint is http://cbc-wilm-agent-public.s3-website-us-east-1.amazonaws.com. S3 static website endpoints DO NOT SUPPORT HTTPS — that is a hard AWS limitation, not a config gap. But bs-tiz.10 notes specify DECK_BASE_URL as 'https://<bucket> or a CloudFront domain' and the whole point of the S3 pivot is the minister opening the link on his phone over the public internet. An emailed http:// link gets a 'Not secure' interstitial on mobile Safari/Chrome, which is a bad look for a link we tell a minister to trust.
design: THREE OPTIONS. (1) Use the REST endpoint instead: https://cbc-wilm-agent-public.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/decks/<date>/index.html. HTTPS works today, public via the existing bucket policy, no new infra. The website config's index_document suffix buys us NOTHING here because bs-tiz.10 already uploads an explicit .../index.html path — the suffix only matters for bare-directory URLs we never emit. Cheapest correct fix; drop the website configuration entirely. (2) CloudFront in front of the bucket: HTTPS + the custom-domain future bs-tiz.10 design already anticipates ('a future CloudFront+custom-domain front keep old links working'), plus it makes the permanent-URL goal real. More moving parts, ~free at this volume. (3) Keep http:// and accept the browser warning — rejected. RECOMMEND (1) now, (2) when a custom domain is wanted; the date-keyed path scheme survives both.
acceptance_criteria: The URL emailed to the minister is https:// and opens clean on a phone with no security interstitial.
notes: DECISION 2026-07-16 (thomas): accept plain http:// for now; not a blocker. Keeping the static website configuration. CORRECTION worth recording, since the decision was initially made on a mistaken premise: static website hosting is NOT required for the generated HTML to reference other objects (images) in the same bucket. The REST endpoint serves any object at https://.s3..amazonaws.com/, and an resolves identically either way — it is just a URL. Website hosting adds only: index-document suffix for bare-directory URLs, custom error documents, and redirect rules. None of those are load-bearing here, since bs-tiz.10 uploads explicit .../index.html paths. So switching to the REST endpoint for HTTPS remains available at ~zero cost whenever wanted; nothing in the deck HTML blocks it.

title: Terraform: S3 deck bucket + agent IAM (infra/)
description: Stand up the public deck bucket that bs-tiz.10/11 publish into, as Terraform in infra/ with the S3 backend in cbc-wilm-agent-private. Creates: (1) aws_s3_bucket cbc-wilm-agent-public configured as a static website; (2) aws_iam_policy cbc-wilm-agent-publisher scoped to that one bucket (ListBucket + GetObject + PutObject, no DeleteObject); (3) aws_iam_user cbc-wilm-agent with that policy attached directly. Outputs: bucket name, website endpoint, policy ARN, user name. APPLIED 2026-07-16 by thomas. Documented in README (Infrastructure section).
design: PUBLIC READ IS A BUCKET POLICY, NOT AN ACL. The original draft used aws_s3_bucket_acl acl=public-read, which grants READ on the BUCKET (list objects) and NOT s3:GetObject on the objects — the website endpoint would have 403'd on every fetch. Replaced with object_ownership=BucketOwnerEnforced (ACLs disabled entirely) + a bucket policy granting anonymous s3:GetObject on arn/*. CONSEQUENCE FOR bs-tiz.10/11: uploads must NOT pass --acl public-read; it now hard-fails with AccessControlListNotSupported. Objects are public via the policy alone. Public access block accordingly relaxes ONLY block_public_policy + restrict_public_buckets; the two ACL flags stay true since ACLs cannot grant anything under BucketOwnerEnforced. Anonymous principals get GetObject only, never ListBucket, so the bucket is not a browsable archive (satisfies the bs-tiz.10 no-listing constraint). NO ROLE IN THE MIDDLE: the agent runs on a self-hosted always-on box (specs/email-agent.md 4.6), so there is no EC2 instance profile to source rotating creds from, and a user-assumes-role hop would add a trust policy without shrinking blast radius (long-lived keys sufficient to assume the role == long-lived keys sufficient to write the bucket). IAM Roles Anywhere would eliminate the standing secret but needs a private CA (~400/mo) — not proportionate here. The policy scoping is the actual control: worst case on a leak is read/write of slide media.
acceptance_criteria: terraform validate passes; apply creates the bucket, policy, and user. Bucket serves an uploaded object publicly over the website endpoint with no --acl flag on upload. Anonymous ListBucket is denied. Agent user can Put and Get but not Delete.
notes: ACCESS KEYS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT IN TERRAFORM. aws_iam_access_key would persist the secret into the state file (in cbc-wilm-agent-private) forever. Key is created by hand in the IAM console and lives ONLY in the agent host's environment (systemd EnvironmentFile, 0600, root-owned — not a .env in the repo). A plan showing a user with no key is CORRECT, not half-finished: Terraform does not track keys and will not report drift on one. Same family as the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY foot-gun on bs-tiz.6 — the AWS SDK has its own credential chain where env vars beat ~/.aws/credentials, so a startup sts:GetCallerIdentity assertion (expect cbc-wilm-agent) is worth baking into the service unit. .gitignore now excludes .terraform/, *.tfstate*, *.tfvars; .terraform.lock.hcl stays TRACKED on purpose (pins provider hashes). AWS_PROFILE must be exported rather than set via provider profile= — the S3 backend resolves credentials independently of the provider block and would otherwise reach for the default profile.

title: Template-sync script (operator-run): upload templates/service/*.png to the S3 asset root
description:
The slide backgrounds are a small SHARED set that changes only when the operator edits or adds a template. A user-run npm script uploads templates/service/*.png to the same S3 asset root the renderer's --asset-base points at. Run MANUALLY when a template changes, NOT per deck. This is the piece that keeps per-deck publishing down to a single HTML upload (bs-tiz.10).

CORRECTED 2026-07-16: the description said '~13 PNGs'. It is actually 23 PNGs / 188MB. The count is higher because the welcome backgrounds have seasonal variants (4 seasons x 3 styles); a given deck uses only one season's worth, but ANY date may be built, so all 23 sync.
acceptance_criteria: Running the script makes every templates/service/*.png reachable under the configured asset base; re-running is idempotent; documented as the operator step to run after changing a template.
notes:
The PNGs this script uploads are the images html2canvas rasterizes at export time. They must be served with Access-Control-Allow-Origin or JPEG export from a cross-origin preview fails with a tainted-canvas SecurityError. CORS OWNERSHIP CORRECTED 2026-07-16: the note originally said this was owned by bs-tiz.10. It is not — the bucket CORS config landed in bs-crp (infra/s3.tf) and the crossorigin="anonymous" half in bs-517. Both are DONE; nothing to do here beyond uploading.

DECISIONS 2026-07-16 (thomas), before implementation:
- IMPLEMENTATION: an npm script wrapping the "aws s3 sync" CLI, NOT scripts/sync-templates.js with @aws-sdk/client-s3. Rationale: the repo has zero AWS npm deps and would gain one; more importantly "aws s3 sync" gives idempotency (size+mtime), parallel upload of 188MB, and Content-Type detection FOR FREE. A hand-rolled PutObject defaults to binary/octet-stream unless ContentType is set explicitly — exactly the bug class that makes images silently not render.
- SIZE/OPTIMIZATION IS OUT OF SCOPE: sync what is on disk today. The 71MB-per-deck page-weight problem is filed as bs-9x5 with the measurements. Keeping it out stops .11 becoming an image-pipeline task and unblocks the bs-tiz.10 + bs-517 live verification now.
- GLOB *.png, NOT *: there is a .DS_Store in templates/service/.
- NO --delete: bs-crp deliberately grants the agent no DeleteObject. The operator may run this with admin creds so --delete would work for them, but the no-delete design is intentional; a renamed template orphaning its old object is harmless. "Idempotent" here means re-running is a no-op, not that it prunes.
- KEY PREFIX must be templates/service/ to match config.deck_asset_base() = ${DECK_BASE_URL}/templates/service (bs-tiz.10). If these drift, every background 404s.

title: Publish tool: upload a generated deck to S3 and return its public URL
description: A tool the agent runs when a deck is ready to share with the minister. It renders (or takes the already-rendered) service-preview.html with the asset base pointed at the S3 template root, uploads the HTML to a date-keyed path in the existing public bucket (e.g. s3://<bucket>/decks/<date>/index.html), and returns the public https URL for the email reply. Per-deck upload is EXACTLY ONE HTML object — templates are synced separately and rarely (see the template-sync issue), and there are no per-deck images and no data-URIs. Bucket, path prefix, and asset base are config (env), not code, because the external URL may change.
design: Content is not sensitive, but do not make it a browsable archive: disable bucket directory listing and use date-keyed, hard-to-enumerate paths. Emit absolute image URLs via the asset-base seam so the HTML renders from the bucket with no local server. Design paths as PERMANENT — an emailed link lives in the mailbox forever; a stable date-based scheme lets a future CloudFront+custom-domain front keep old links working.
acceptance_criteria: Running the tool for a deck uploads a single HTML object, prints the public URL, and that URL renders with correct backgrounds in a browser with no local server running. ALSO: the bucket (or its CDN front) returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin on template-image responses, and JPEG export via the Export button is VERIFIED from the hosted S3 URL — not just locally — because cross-origin template images can taint the html2canvas canvas and make canvas.toBlob() throw a SecurityError (export fails while the deck still looks correct on screen).
notes: ENV/INVOCATION design (2026-07-16, confirmed w/ thomas). Single origin var DECK_BASE_URL = public bucket/CDN origin (e.g. https://<bucket> or a CloudFront domain). The publish tool COMPOSES from it and passes --asset-base EXPLICITLY as a CLI arg to build-deck.js — never relies on .env bleeding into the Node subprocess (nothing loads .env into Node's process.env; the env-file plumbing is Python-side only): asset-base = ${DECK_BASE_URL}/templates/service ; deck link = ${DECK_BASE_URL}/decks/<date>/index.html . PUBLIC_BASE_URL is REMOVED/superseded by DECK_BASE_URL (update .env.example + agent config.py public_base_url->deck_base_url). DECK_ASSET_BASE (read by build-deck.js, bs-tiz.9) stays ONLY as a manual/dev script override, documented in .env.example as optional; the tool does not use it. The templates path (/templates/service) must match where bs-tiz.11 uploads.  ||  IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-16 (commit 2a03bed). agent/src/email_agent/publish.py: publish_deck(deck_json) -> {url,bucket,key,date}; SDK tool mcp__deck__publish_deck wired into harness via mcp_servers={'deck': ...}. DECK_BASE_URL/DECK_BUCKET/DECK_PREFIX in config + .env.example; PUBLIC_BASE_URL removed. 16 unit tests (S3 client + subprocess injected) incl. one that runs the REAL build-deck.js so a --asset-base rename cannot pass silently. KEY DESIGN: publish RE-RENDERS from deck JSON to a temp dir rather than uploading passages/<date>/service-preview.html — that local file is built with the default /templates/service asset base and would host with every background 404. Local preview left untouched. config deck_* fields use default_factory (a bare os.getenv default is evaluated once at IMPORT, so Config() would ignore env — same reason subject_pattern already did this).  ||  VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-16 (partial, per thomas's call to defer): example deck published to s3://cbc-wilm-agent-public/decks/2026-06-28/index.html; curl returns 200, Content-Type text/html; charset=utf-8, Cache-Control public max-age=300 (300s NOT immutable, deliberately — a corrected deck re-publishes to the SAME url and must not serve stale). HTML carries absolute bucket-origin img srcs, 37 crossorigin=anonymous, ZERO local /templates paths. STILL OUTSTANDING (both need bs-tiz.11 templates in the bucket): (1) backgrounds actually rendering, (2) JPEG Export from the hosted URL + from a local preview pointed at the S3 base — converges with bs-517's remaining criterion. CAVEAT: local smoke test ran as ACCOUNT ROOT (arn:aws:iam::867500253271:root), NOT the cbc-wilm-agent user, so it did NOT exercise the scoped IAM policy — root can write anything, so a policy bug would not have shown. Real credential check must happen on the agent host.

title: build-deck.js: configurable media asset base (decouple image paths from serving root)
description: The renderer hardcodes image src as /templates/service/ (the bg() helper at scripts/build-deck.js:463), which assumes the deck is served from the same origin/root as the template PNGs. To publish decks to object storage (S3) independently of where the agent runs, the renderer must emit media paths from a CONFIGURED base. Add a --asset-base CLI flag (and matching env, e.g. DECK_ASSET_BASE) that prefixes every media reference. When set to a full origin (e.g. https:///templates/service) the emitted become ABSOLUTE URLs, so the HTML renders correctly no matter where the file itself is opened (email client, bucket root, sub-path, local disk). This is the single seam that decouples the deck HTML from its serving location.
design: Change only bg() and thread the base through. Default MUST remain the literal '/templates/service' so existing local Express serving AND the golden tests (tests/build-deck.test.js + tests/golden/*) stay byte-for-byte identical when the flag is unset. Absolute-URL mode is opt-in via the flag/env.
acceptance_criteria: bg() reads from a configurable base; with the flag unset the golden output is reproduced byte-for-byte; with a full-URL base every is an absolute URL; a unit test pins both modes.
notes: Export interaction: once the asset base points at a cross-origin S3 URL, the background images become cross-origin. The Export button's html2canvas bakes those images into each JPEG, so the bucket MUST send Access-Control-Allow-Origin or canvas.toBlob() throws (tainted canvas). Same-origin '/templates/...' (the default) never hits this; it only appears once decks are hosted. CORS config + a hosted-export test live on bs-tiz.10.
close_reason: Implemented --asset-base + DECK_ASSET_BASE; default byte-identical (golden tests green), full-origin yields absolute URLs, trailing slash normalized; verified via npm test (16/16) and CLI e2e. Unblocks bs-tiz.10/.11.

title: Eval: prove the model adds a caesura when the report asks for one
description:
The caesura loop has two halves. The SCRIPT half is proven (tests/build-deck.test.js: an unmarked over-wide line shrinks the song and the report names the line + the fix). The MODEL half is NOT.

In the 7/12 eval the agent looked up two new hymns and both happened to fit at 60px, so report.typography was empty and it was never asked to mark anything. So we have not yet seen the model: (a) read a 'shrunk' typography entry, (b) place a '|' at the line's sense-break in songs/*.md, (c) rebuild and get back to 60px, (d) mention the split in its reply so the operator can move a badly-placed marker.

That loop is the whole reason the mechanism exists — the script measures, the model judges. Until it is exercised, 'the model proposes the caesura' is a design intention, not an observed behaviour.

HOW: add an eval fixture whose flowchart names a hymn with a genuinely long line that the agent must look up fresh (so it writes the song file itself). Assert the resulting song file contains a '|', the report's typography kind is 'caesura' not 'shrunk', and the size is 60px. Consider also asserting the break lands at a sense-break rather than the midpoint — probably by pinning the expected split for that one known hymn.
acceptance_criteria: An eval shows the agent placing a caesura in a song file it wrote, keeping the song at 60px, and mentioning the split in its reply.

title: Agent output can be blocked by content filtering (verbatim lyrics)
description:
An eval run of the 7/5 flowchart died mid-run with 'API Error: 400 Output blocked by content filtering policy'. The agent sent NO reply; the run simply ended.

TRIGGER (probable): the agent's core job is reproducing song lyrics verbatim into songs/*.md. The 7/5 flowchart is all patriotic hymns (Star-Spangled Banner, Battle Hymn of the Republic, America the Beautiful, My Country 'Tis of Thee). Long verbatim lyric output looks like copyrighted-material reproduction to an output filter. NONDETERMINISTIC — the same eval passed twice before this and 6/8 tests passed on the failing run.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the one failure mode that produces SILENCE. The minister emails on Saturday, the agent dies, and nothing comes back. The dispatcher's failure path (bs-tiz.2) should catch it — agent error -> thread out of in-flight -> 'I hit an error' reply — but that path has NOT been exercised against this specific failure, and if the error arrives as an assistant TextBlock rather than an exception, the harness may treat it as a normal (empty) completion instead of an error. VERIFY THAT.

MITIGATIONS TO CONSIDER:
1. Confirm harness.py raises AgentError on a filtered/errored run rather than completing silently. The run must reach the dispatcher's failure path.
2. Lyrics are written to songs/*.md with the Write tool — consider whether writing them via a tool call (rather than emitting them in prose) is less likely to trip the filter, and prefer that path.
3. The reply itself should never quote lyrics back; it should reference songs by title.
4. Retry once on a filtered run before giving up.

tests/eval/eval_harness.py:EvalRun.error now surfaces this so it stops masquerading as 'the agent chose not to reply'.
acceptance_criteria: A content-filtered agent run reaches the dispatcher's failure path and results in an 'I hit an error' reply to the minister, never silence. The trigger is understood and reduced.
notes:
SEVERITY REDUCED after checking the production path — it is NOT silence.

A content-filtered run ends without calling send_reply or skip_reply, which trips the 'if not terminal' guard at harness.py:151 -> AgentError -> the dispatcher's failure path (bs-tiz.2): thread marked failed, claim released, message retried on the next tick. This is exactly the case bs-tiz.4's design note anticipated ('Deciding NOTHING is the error, because the dispatcher's commit boundary would drop the request silently'). The guard earns its keep here.

So the real-world behaviour is: the run dies, and the next heartbeat retries it. Since the filter is nondeterministic, a retry will often succeed. Remaining work is therefore hardening, not rescue:
1. The retry is currently unbounded-ish — confirm a filtered thread cannot retry forever, and that a repeatedly-failing thread eventually emails 'I hit an error' rather than looping quietly.
2. Reduce the trigger: prefer writing lyrics via the Write tool over emitting them in prose, and never quote lyrics back in the reply body (reference songs by title).

Observed once in 8 eval runs (~12%), on the all-patriotic-hymns 7/5 flowchart.

title: His Name Is Jesus: song identity unconfirmed, lyrics are a placeholder
description: songs/his-name-is-jesus.md has a literal placeholder string '(paste lyrics here — song identity unconfirmed)' inside a '## Verse 1' section. Several worship songs share this title. Under the pre-bs-c16 flow an 'all sections' default would have projected that placeholder text onto the sanctuary screen — a direct violation of the skill's cardinal rule. scripts/build-deck.js now detects placeholder sections (explicit request = validation error; default = skipped + reported), so the immediate danger is contained. Still needs a human: confirm which song the church actually sings and paste the licensed lyrics.
acceptance_criteria: The song file contains the correct, confirmed lyrics, or is deleted if the church does not sing it.

title: Migrate gen_service from legacy command to a SKILL.md skill
description: gen_service currently lives at .claude/commands/gen_service.md — the Agent SDK auto-loads this, but the docs flag .claude/commands/*.md as the LEGACY format and recommend .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md for new custom skills. Migrate gen_service to .claude/skills/gen_service/SKILL.md so both the interactive Claude Code workflow and the email agent (Agent SDK) invoke it via the supported path. Natural companion to the bs-c16/bs-ixn rework since we're already restructuring the skill's contract; do it in the same pass to avoid touching gen_service twice.
acceptance_criteria: gen_service exists as .claude/skills/gen_service/SKILL.md and loads/runs from both the Claude Code CLI and a claude-agent-sdk query; the legacy command file is removed or reduced to a thin pointer; existing behavior is unchanged.
notes:
DISCOVERY from the bs-tiz.7 spike: ClaudeAgentOptions has a DEDICATED 'skills' field alongside setting_sources (verified against the installed claude-agent-sdk 0.2.116). Look at it before doing this migration — it may let the harness load skills WITHOUT pulling in all project settings via setting_sources=['project'], which is currently how the agent sees .claude/.

Also relevant: the legacy .claude/commands/gen_service.md was substantially rewritten by bs-c16 (it now emits deck JSON and shells out to scripts/build-deck.js instead of hand-writing HTML). Pair this migration with the bs-ixn batch-mode rework rather than doing it standalone — otherwise the file gets rewritten twice.

Confirmed working today: with setting_sources=['project'], an SDK query sees gen_service, gen_slides and prep_sermon. So the migration is an improvement, not a prerequisite — nothing is broken as-is.

title: Deployment host: always-on local box for the agent (CRON gate + dispatcher + agent); deck delivery decoupled to S3
description: REVISED 2026-07-15 (see specs/deck-publishing.md). The agent still needs one small ALWAYS-ON host — the user's home server / Raspberry Pi — to run the CRON heartbeat gate, the dispatcher, and the agent against a shared filesystem. What changed: deck DELIVERY is no longer served off this host. The original plan co-located an Express server and wrote service-preview.html into a served passages/ tree, with the reply link = https://<host>/passages/<date>/... and explicitly 'no upload step', reached by the minister over a tailnet. That is reversed: decks now PUBLISH to a public S3 bucket (bs-tiz.10) and the minister opens them on his phone over the public internet, so (a) the host does NOT need to serve decks to anyone but the operator, and (b) the minister needs NO tailnet/VPN access at all. The host may still serve the Bible Scroller app itself for the operator, but that is now separable from deck delivery. There IS a deliberate upload step now (bs-tiz.10 + bs-tiz.11).
acceptance_criteria: An always-on host runs the CRON gate, dispatcher, and agent against the shared filesystem with subscription OAuth auth (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset). A generated deck reaches the minister via a public S3 URL (bs-tiz.10), openable on a phone with no tailnet membership. Serving the scroller app to the operator is optional and independent of deck delivery.
notes: AUTH on the host: authenticate the Agent SDK with a subscription OAuth token from 'claude setup-token' set as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. FOOT-GUN: ensure ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is UNSET in the host/service environment — if present it silently wins over the OAuth token and bills a pay-per-token API account instead of the subscription. Bake an env-scrub / assertion into the service unit. (Subscription-vs-API decision recorded on the epic bs-tiz.)  ||  PUBLIC_BASE_URL (tagged here in .env.example) is superseded by DECK_BASE_URL, owned by bs-tiz.10 (see specs/deck-publishing.md).

title: gen_service: disambiguate 'special music' segment vs congregational praise
description: The taxonomy is tangled: special music is a SEGMENT (choir/soloist performs, usually title+performer, congregation does not read), while praise songs are congregational (title + lyric slides). In the worked example His Name Is Jesus was mislabeled 'Special Music' — a small model would copy that. Clarify the distinction and the resulting slide treatment/background for each.
acceptance_criteria: Skill clearly separates the special-music segment from congregational song handling, including background and whether lyrics are shown; example corrected.
notes:
CONCRETE EVIDENCE (2026-07-12, found while adding the build-deck golden test in bs-66k): the ambiguity is real and already live in the reference deck.

examples/2026-06-28.deck.json encodes 'His Name Is Jesus' as type=special_music. The script therefore renders slide 22 on choir.png (what gen_service.md documents for special_music). The HAND-BUILT passages/2026-06-28/service-preview.html renders that same slide on praise-2.png — the congregational-praise background.

So the epic's claim that the example deck 'reproduces the hand-built 36-slide deck identically' is FALSE by exactly one line: slide 22's background img. Everything else is byte-identical (verified by diff). Both versions carry the same 'Special Music' label and the same scrim, so only the background disagrees.

This is the bs-fdn question in miniature: was 'His Name Is Jesus' special music (a performed number) or congregational praise (the room sings)? It is currently BOTH, depending on which artifact you read. Needs a human answer — it is a liturgical/aesthetic call, not a code bug. Whichever way it goes, fix examples/2026-06-28.deck.json and re-record the golden (npm run test:update).

Related: bs-1nn (that same song's identity/lyrics are unconfirmed) — the two are probably one conversation with the minister of music.
close_reason:
RESOLVED by examples/flowcharts.md + user confirmation 2026-07-12.

THE RULE: 'Tehillah' is the church's PRAISE TEAM — a marker for CONGREGATIONAL singing, not a performer. So in a flowchart:
  - 'Choir: <title>' and 'Quartet' => special_music (a performed number; needs a song title AND a performer)
  - 'Tehillah: <title>' and the bare song titles following it => congregational praise (type=song)

Applied: examples/2026-06-28.deck.json had 'His Name Is Jesus' as special_music; it is congregational praise (type=song). Fixed and the golden re-recorded. This also removed the last inconsistency in the reference deck: the hand-built HTML rendered that slide on the praise-2 background but with special music's scrim and label. The script is now self-consistent (praise-2, no scrim — matching every other praise slide in the deck — and an amber VERIFY flag, correct because that song's lyrics are genuinely unconfirmed: bs-1nn).

This rule must be encoded in gen_service's non-interactive mode (bs-ixn).

title: gen_service: explicit songs/ lookup step
description: The skill never explicitly tells the model to list songs/ and match by slug/title before resolving a song; a small model may skip the library or invent a slug. Add an explicit first step: enumerate songs/, match the requested title to a slug, and only then fall through to fetch/PD/report logic.
acceptance_criteria: Skill instructs listing songs/ and matching before any fetch; slug-matching rule (title normalization) documented.

title: Songs library: pre-segment stanzas and store the sung sequence
description: Two runtime judgment calls are unreliable on a small model: (a) splitting a stanza that would overflow the 60px floor 'at a natural break', and (b) 'include the refrain after each verse if that's how it's sung'. Move both to library-authoring time. Each song file should carry stanzas already sized to fit one slide and an explicit default sung sequence (encoding refrain placement), so at runtime the model just follows section order — no width estimation, no hymnody judgment.
acceptance_criteria: Song file format documents a per-slide stanza guarantee and a default sequence field; gen_service follows the stored sequence instead of deciding refrain placement; existing seed songs migrated.

title: README cleanup: prerequisites section + clear map of the repo's subsystems
description: The README is currently a mess and does not reflect that this repo now contains several distinct subsystems. Rework it. Two concrete jobs: (1) A PREREQUISITES section covering what an operator/deployer needs to set up — Node, the agent's Python/uv env, subscription OAuth token (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN) with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset, and the S3 publishing config: bucket, asset-base/DECK_BASE_URL env, disabled directory listing, and CRUCIALLY the bucket CORS config (Access-Control-Allow-Origin on template images) that the JPEG Export button depends on (see bs-tiz.9/.10/.11 and specs/deck-publishing.md). (2) A clear up-front DISTINCTION between the things this repo does, which currently blur together: (a) the Bible Scroller presentation app itself (server.js + index.html + app.js — the original scroller); (b) the Claude skills (gen_service, gen_slides, prep_sermon) that generate slide decks / sermon material; (c) the deterministic deck renderer (scripts/build-deck.js) and song library (songs/); (d) the email Agent subsystem (agent/, CRON gate + dispatcher + SDK harness) documented in specs/email-agent.md; (e) deck publishing to S3 (specs/deck-publishing.md). Point readers at the two specs rather than duplicating them.
acceptance_criteria: README opens with a short map distinguishing the scroller app, the skills, the deck renderer, the email agent, and S3 publishing, each with a one-line 'what it is' and a pointer to its spec where one exists. A Prerequisites section lists the env/setup for running the agent and publishing decks, including the S3 CORS requirement for JPEG export. No subsystem is left implicit.

title: Harden gate against agent-authored mail (reply-loop defence-in-depth)
description:
The reply-loop bug (agent replying to its own replies) was fixed on 2026-07-11 at the DISPATCHER layer: tools.send_reply records the sent message id via store.mark_agent_sent(), so is_processed() rejects it. That is correct and is covered by a mutation-checked regression test (agent/tests/test_reply_loop.py).

But the guard is only in the dispatcher, which leaves two rough edges:
1. The gate still emits agent-authored messages as 'actionable' on every tick and the dispatcher discards them — correct but wasteful (observed: gate saw 3 actionable, dispatcher processed 0).
2. The guard is STATE-dependent. Wiping or losing state.db would make the agent's own past replies look like fresh requests again and re-trigger the loop on an existing thread. The state store is bookkeeping, so treating it as a safety mechanism is fragile.

Harden at the gate so the invariant holds without state: e.g. skip messages whose From is the authenticated user AND that carry the SENT label (safe in production, where the minister's mail is inbound-only), or track authored Message-IDs, or bound the query to messages newer than the thread's last agent reply. Note the self-email test case defeats naive From/label filtering — every message carries both SENT and INBOX.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting state.db and re-running the heartbeat against an already-answered thread does not send a duplicate reply.
notes:
LARGELY ADDRESSED 2026-07-12, but by steering rather than by a gate — which is the better fix. The original framing of this issue (harden the deterministic filter) accepted a flawed premise: the agent had no way to judge for itself, because (a) it was handed a single msg_id, never the thread, and (b) the system prompt COMPELLED a reply ('never finish silently'), so declining was structurally impossible. Authorship tracking was therefore load-bearing safety, which is too much weight for bookkeeping.

Now: get_thread gives the agent the whole conversation with authorship as an explicit HINT (documented as fallible), and skip_reply makes 'no reply is warranted' a first-class terminal outcome. The harness accepts send_reply OR skip_reply; only deciding NOTHING is an error.

VERIFIED LIVE with state.db DELETED (every authored_by_agent flag false): the agent read the thread, recognised its own prior replies from their content, and declined 3/3 times — explicitly reasoning 'replying again would just be me answering myself' and 'to avoid perpetuating the loop'. No mail sent. This is precisely the state-loss scenario this issue was filed for.

REMAINING (why this stays open, at lower priority): the gate still emits agent-authored messages every tick and the dispatcher discards them — correct but wasteful, and each one that reaches the agent costs a Sonnet call to decide 'no'. Worth a cheap gate-level filter as an efficiency measure, but it is no longer a SAFETY issue: correctness now rests on the agent's judgment, with the store as a cheap fast-path and a hint.

title: Vendor html2canvas locally (drop the cdnjs dependency in the slide template)
description: The service-slides template loads html2canvas from cdnjs (the export-to-image button). In the S3 + phone delivery model the CDN works fine (internet is guaranteed for the minister, and the export button is an operator tool run locally with internet), so this is NOT on the critical path — captured for completeness. Vendoring the one file removes the last external dependency, so a deck renders and exports with no internet at all (e.g. if ever served from an offline box).
acceptance_criteria: The slide template references a locally-served/vendored html2canvas; no request to cdnjs.cloudflare.com; export button still works offline.
